items.title: Sit Less, Move More: A Quasi-Experimental Benchmarking (QEB) of Machine Learning for Reliable Activity Classification
items.authors: Srinivasa Reddy Arekuti; Sai Mounika Chintalapudi; Ganga Basyal
items.tldr: Benchmarks machine-learning approaches for reliable human-activity classification using a quasi-experimental design, with practical relevance for movement and wellness applications.
items.citation: Arekuti, S. R., Chintalapudi, S. M., & Basyal, G. (2026). Sit less, move more: A quasi-experimental benchmarking (QEB) of machine learning for reliable activity classification. MWAIS 2026 Proceedings, 38.

items.title: Impact of Data Characteristics on the Effectiveness of Multi-Stage Transfer Learning Using MRI Medical Images
items.venue: Dakota State University, PhD in Information Systems
items.tldr: Develops and evaluates a multi-stage transfer-learning approach for MRI classification, showing how image quantity, quality, resolution, contrast, noise, and domain differences affect model performance.
items.citation: Basyal, G. P. (2025). Impact of data characteristics on the effectiveness of multi-stage transfer learning using MRI medical images (Doctoral dissertation, Dakota State University).

items.title: Development of CNN Architectures Using Transfer Learning Methods for Medical Image Classification
items.authors: Ganga Prasad Basyal; David Zeng; Bhaskar Prasad Rimal
items.tldr: Maps the development of CNN and transfer-learning architectures for medical-image classification and identifies key considerations for selecting effective state-of-the-art models.
items.citation: Basyal, G. P., Zeng, D., & Rimal, B. P. (2024). Development of CNN architectures using transfer learning methods for medical image classification. arXiv. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2410.16711

items.title: Navigating the Docker Ecosystem: A Comprehensive Taxonomy and Survey
items.authors: Prathamesh Muzumdar; Amol Bhosale; Ganga Prasad Basyal; George Kurian
items.venue: Asian Journal of Research in Computer Science, 17(1)
items.tldr: Organizes the Docker ecosystem into a practical taxonomy, compares container architectures, and highlights research gaps around scalable and portable microservices.
items.citation: Muzumdar, P., Bhosale, A., Basyal, G. P., & Kurian, G. (2024). Navigating the Docker ecosystem: A comprehensive taxonomy and survey. Asian Journal of Research in Computer Science, 17(1). https://doi.org/10.9734/AJRCOS/2024/v17i1411

items.title: A Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) Semantic Text Analytics Approach to Explore Topical Features in Charity Crowdfunding Campaigns
items.authors: Prathamesh Muzumdar; George Kurian; Ganga Prasad Basyal
items.venue: Asian Journal of Economics, Business and Accounting, 24(1)
items.tldr: Uses LDA topic modeling and a random-forest classifier to uncover themes in charity-campaign narratives and connect textual and numeric features to campaign success.
items.citation: Muzumdar, P., Kurian, G., & Basyal, G. P. (2024). A latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA) semantic text analytics approach to explore topical features in charity crowdfunding campaigns. Asian Journal of Economics, Business and Accounting, 24(1). https://doi.org/10.9734/AJEBA/2024/v24i11207

items.title: Risk of AI in Healthcare: A Comprehensive Literature Review and Study Framework
items.authors: Apoorva Muley; Prathamesh Muzumdar; George Kurian; Ganga Prasad Basyal
items.venue: Asian Journal of Medicine and Health, 21(10)
items.tldr: Synthesizes 39 studies into three major healthcare-AI risk categories—clinical data, technical, and socio-ethical—and proposes a framework for future empirical research.
items.citation: Muley, A., Muzumdar, P., Kurian, G., & Basyal, G. P. (2023). Risk of AI in healthcare: A comprehensive literature review and study framework. Asian Journal of Medicine and Health, 21(10). https://doi.org/10.9734/AJMAH/2023/v21i10903

items.title: Econometrics Modelling Approach to Examine the Effect of STEM Policy Changes on Asian Students’ Enrollment Decision in USA
items.authors: Prathamesh Muzumdar; George Kurian; Ganga Prasad Basyal; Apoorva Muley
items.venue: Asian Journal of Education and Social Studies, 48(2)
items.tldr: Applies a difference-in-differences design to examine how the 2008 STEM OPT extension influenced Asian international students’ decisions to enroll in U.S. STEM programs.
items.citation: Muzumdar, P., Kurian, G., Basyal, G. P., & Muley, A. (2023). Econometrics modelling approach to examine the effect of STEM policy changes on Asian students’ enrollment decision in USA. Asian Journal of Education and Social Studies, 48(2). https://doi.org/10.9734/AJESS/2023/v48i21062

items.title: An Empirical Comparison of Machine Learning Models for Students’ Mental Health Illness Assessment
items.authors: Prathamesh Muzumdar; Ganga Prasad Basyal; Piyush Vyas
items.venue: Asian Journal of Computer and Information Systems, 10(1)
items.tldr: Compares nine machine-learning classifiers for student mental-health assessment and identifies XGBoost plus social support, learning environment, and childhood adversity as important signals.
items.citation: Muzumdar, P., Basyal, G. P., & Vyas, P. (2022). An empirical comparison of machine learning models for students’ mental health illness assessment. Asian Journal of Computer and Information Systems, 10(1). https://doi.org/10.24203/AJCIS.v10i1.6882

items.title: Automated Classification of Societal Sentiments on Twitter With Machine Learning
items.authors: Piyush Vyas; Martin Reisslein; Bhaskar Prasad Rimal; Gitika Vyas; Ganga Prasad Basyal; Prathamesh Muzumdar
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Technology and Society
items.tldr: Builds a hybrid lexicon-plus-supervised-learning pipeline for COVID-era Twitter sentiment classification; an LSTM achieved the strongest reported classification performance.
items.citation: Vyas, P., Reisslein, M., Rimal, B. P., Vyas, G., Basyal, G. P., & Muzumdar, P. (2021). Automated classification of societal sentiments on Twitter with machine learning. IEEE Transactions on Technology and Society. https://doi.org/10.1109/TTS.2021.3108963

items.title: Comparative Study of CNN Models for Brain Tumor Classification: Computational Efficiency Versus Accuracy
items.authors: Ganga Prasad Basyal; David Zeng; Dave Bishop; Bhaskar Prasad Rimal
items.tldr: Compares leading CNN architectures for brain-tumor classification and frames model selection as an accuracy-versus-computational-cost decision-support problem.
items.citation: Basyal, G. P., Zeng, D., Bishop, D., & Rimal, B. P. (2021). Comparative study of CNN models for brain tumor classification: Computational efficiency versus accuracy. AMCIS 2021 Proceedings.

items.title: Moderating Effects of Retail Operations and Hard-Sell Sales Techniques on Salesperson’s Interpersonal Skills and Customer Repurchase Intention
items.authors: Prathamesh Muzumdar; Ganga Prasad Basyal; Piyush Vyas
items.tldr: Shows how operational friction and hard-sell practices can weaken the positive relationship between salesperson interpersonal skills and customers’ intention to repurchase.
items.citation: Muzumdar, P., Basyal, G. P., & Vyas, P. (2020). Moderating effects of retail operations and hard-sell sales techniques on salesperson’s interpersonal skills and customer repurchase intention. Journal of Management Research, 13(1). https://doi.org/10.5296/jmr.v13i1.18044

items.title: Antecedents of Student Retention: A Predictive Modelling Approach
items.authors: Prathamesh Muzumdar; Ganga Prasad Basyal; Piyush Vyas
items.venue: International Journal of Contemporary Research and Review, 11(11)
items.tldr: Uses component analysis, multiple regression, and logistic regression to examine how peer effectiveness, academic progress, and advising shape university-student retention.
items.citation: Muzumdar, P., Basyal, G. P., & Vyas, P. (2020). Antecedents of student retention: A predictive modelling approach. International Journal of Contemporary Research and Review, 11(11). https://doi.org/10.15520/ijcrr.v11i11.860

items.title: A Systematic Review of Natural Language Processing for Knowledge Management in Healthcare
items.authors: Ganga Prasad Basyal; Bhaskar Prasad Rimal; David Zeng
items.tldr: Reviews how natural-language processing supports knowledge management in healthcare and organizes the field’s methods, applications, and research opportunities.
items.citation: Basyal, G. P., Rimal, B. P., & Zeng, D. (2020). A systematic review of natural language processing for knowledge management in healthcare. Computer Science & Information Technology. https://doi.org/10.5121/csit.2020.100921

items.title: Impact of Data Quality and Quantity on Its Effectiveness on Multi-Stage Transfer Learning Using MRI Medical Images
items.tldr: Proposes a four-stage transfer-learning design to investigate how MRI image quality, quantity, domain adaptation, and computational complexity affect medical-image models.
